name: com.outputcharts/mcp
title: Output Charts
description: Dashboards from JSON with a stable public link; sign up, build and keep fresh, all as tools.

tools.name: signup
tools.description: Create an account for a person's email and a Manage key for this agent; the person claims the account from the claim link. 5 per IP and 300 in all a day. Creates an account for the person's email, with a seven-day Solo trial and a Manage key for this agent, and emails them a claim link. The trial is once per person: a mailbox that had one (plus tags and Gmail dots count as the same mailbox), or a second sign-up from one network within 30 days, gets the account on Free with no trial, and the response says so in fix. 409 email_taken when the address already has an account: its owner makes a key under Account → API keys instead. Limited to 5 sign-ups per IP and 300 in all a day (429 rate_limited).

email.description: The person's address. The account is theirs; the claim email goes there.

agentName.description: The agent or product making the account, such as Claude Code. Names the key and is mentioned in the claim email.

useCase.description: What the person wants a dashboard for, in a sentence.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The key, its owner's tier and dashboard allowance, and the limits. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: create_api_key
tools.description: Create a narrower key: push only, or bound to one dashboard. Shown once. A Push key bound to one dashboard is the right key for a CI job or a cron that only sends data. Solo owners hold at most five live keys. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

scope.description: push: send data and read visuals. manage: everything this key can do.

dashboardId.description: Bind the key to one of the owner's dashboards: it then reaches only that dashboard's visuals.

tools.name: get_checkout_link
tools.description: A Stripe Checkout link that puts this account on Solo; give it to the account's owner. Works after the trial has ended, when every other call answers requires_solo. Works on Free and after the trial has ended: this is the call to make after a 403 requires_solo. The link is a hosted Stripe page for the account's owner to complete; calls work again as soon as they pay. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

interval.description: Which Solo price the session is for.

promotionCode.description: A Stripe promotion code to apply, such as a launch code the person was given; without one the Checkout page offers its own code field.

tools.name: list_dashboards
tools.description: The owner's dashboards, oldest first; ref narrows to the one with that ref. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

ref.description: A slug you choose, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -. Unique per owner for dashboards and per dashboard for visuals, and set once. Create with a ref so a later run finds the same object instead of making a duplicate.

tools.name: create_dashboard
tools.description: Create a dashboard; with a ref already in use, return that dashboard with created false. One call can make a live page: send visuals and publish true, and the answer carries the dashboard's url. A ref already used by one of the owner's dashboards returns that dashboard, unchanged, with created false; its visuals are then created or found by their own refs, so a run cut short is finished by the next one. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

ref.description: A slug you choose, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -. Unique per owner for dashboards and per dashboard for visuals, and set once. Create with a ref so a later run finds the same object instead of making a duplicate.

visuals.description: Created in order, each as POST /v1/dashboards/{id}/visuals would, so give every visual a ref when the dashboard has one.

size.description: Defaults to the type's default size. Width and height within the type's limits, which describe_visual_types lists per type with the widths the editor offers.

ref.description: A slug you choose, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -. Unique per owner for dashboards and per dashboard for visuals, and set once. Create with a ref so a later run finds the same object instead of making a duplicate.

publish.description: Make the page public for anyone with the link, as POST /v1/dashboards/{id}/publish would.

shareWith.description: People who may view the dashboard after signing in with these addresses, each made as POST /v1/dashboards/{id}/shares would and emailed the link: view-only, and the dashboard stays private unless publish is true too.

dryRun.description: Check everything and write nothing; answers 200 { dryRun: true } or the error the real call would give.

tools.name: get_dashboard
tools.description: A dashboard with its visual count and its visuals in reading order. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: update_dashboard
tools.description: Change title, description or scheme; set a ref once on a dashboard that has none. Send only the fields to change. A ref can be set once, on a dashboard that has none. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

ref.description: A slug you choose, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -. Unique per owner for dashboards and per dashboard for visuals, and set once. Create with a ref so a later run finds the same object instead of making a duplicate.

indexable.description: False takes the public page out of search engines, the gallery and the sitemap and mints a claim token (claimToken on the dashboard) for the person it was built for; true puts it back and drops the token. A dashboard already out keeps its token.

isShowcase.description: True lists a published dashboard in the gallery, where search engines may index it (409 not_public on a dashboard that is not published); false takes it out, leaving the page to people with the link. Unpublishing clears it.

tools.name: reorder_visuals
tools.description: Put every visual of the dashboard in a new reading order and reflow. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

visualIds.description: Every visual of the dashboard exactly once, in the new reading order.

tools.name: publish_dashboard
tools.description: Make the dashboard public for anyone with the link, under the same rules and caps as the app; listing it in the gallery is isShowcase on PATCH. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: unpublish_dashboard
tools.description: Make the dashboard private again. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: share_dashboard
tools.description: Give one person view access after they sign in with this address, and email them the link; an address that already has a share comes back with created false. View-only. A person with an account sees the dashboard at once; anyone else has the share attached the moment they sign up or sign in with that address. The same address again returns the existing share with created false and sends nothing. The dashboard need not be public: this is how named people see a private one. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

email.description: The person who may view the dashboard after signing in with this address. They get an email with the link.

tools.name: list_shares
tools.description: The dashboard's shares, oldest first, each with its status. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: revoke_share
tools.description: Revoke one share: the person loses access at once. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: create_visual
tools.description: Create a visual with its document, size and position; with a ref already in this dashboard, return that visual with created false. A ref already used in this dashboard returns that visual, unchanged, with created false. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

size.description: Defaults to the type's default size. Width and height within the type's limits, which describe_visual_types lists per type with the widths the editor offers.

position.description: Index in reading order; absent or past the end puts the visual last.

ref.description: A slug you choose, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -. Unique per owner for dashboards and per dashboard for visuals, and set once. Create with a ref so a later run finds the same object instead of making a duplicate.

tools.name: batch_update
tools.description: Replace the documents of several visuals at once, keyed by each visual's ref. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

data.description: The new documents, keyed by the ref of the visual each one replaces, so one call keeps a whole dashboard fresh. Each is read as PUT /v1/visuals/{id}/data reads it (whole document, numeric strings coerced). Every entry is tried in the order sent: 200 when all were written, 422 batch_failed with the same results when any was not.

additionalProperties.description: The visual's whole JSON document, valid for the visual's type: the rules per type are on create_visual's document and in describe_visual_types; get_visual shows the current one.

tools.name: get_visual
tools.description: One visual with its type, title, ref, size, position and document. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: update_visual
tools.description: Change title, document or size; set a ref once on a visual that has none. The type cannot change. Send only the fields to change. The type cannot change; a ref can be set once, on a visual that has none. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

document.description: The visual's whole JSON document, valid for the visual's type: the rules per type are on create_visual's document and in describe_visual_types; get_visual shows the current one.

size.description: Width and height within the type's limits, which describe_visual_types lists per type with the widths the editor offers.

ref.description: A slug you choose, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -. Unique per owner for dashboards and per dashboard for visuals, and set once. Create with a ref so a later run finds the same object instead of making a duplicate.

tools.name: delete_visual
tools.description: Delete the visual, its pointer and its ref, then reflow the rest. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: push_visual_data
tools.description: Replace the visual's document; the body is the document itself, valid for the visual's type. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

tools.name: append_rows
tools.description: Add rows to the end of the visual's data and drop the oldest past keepLast; the visual's settings are unchanged. Adds rows to a line, area, bar, bar-horizontal, scatter, table or map visual; its settings (xKey, series, columns) are unchanged, and numeric strings are coerced as on push. On a map the rows merge by region: a row whose code matches an existing one replaces it, the others are added, and keepLast is ignored. A kpi, gauge, pie, funnel or markdown visual has no row list: replace its document with PUT /v1/visuals/{id}/data instead. Over HTTP keepLast may also go in the query string (?keepLast=7), and the body may be text/csv: the header row is the keys the visual's rows have. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

rows.description: Added after the rows the visual holds, in order.

items.description: One data row, with the keys the visual's rows have: the xKey and the series keys, or the column keys.

keepLast.description: Keep only the newest keepLast rows after the append, dropping the oldest. The type's cap applies in any case: line 500, area 500, bar 500, bar-horizontal 500, scatter 500, table 200, map 4000 rows.

tools.name: describe_visual_types
tools.description: The visual types, each with its document rules, an example document and its size limits; the widths, schemes and limits.
